newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares up, moderate U.S. rate hike seen.
newsitem.headline: German shares up, moderate U.S. rate hike seen.

text.p: German shares advanced in tentative bourse trade on Tuesday, buoyed by Wall Street's overnight gains and quietly confident that an expected U.S. rate hike later today will not exceed 25 basis points.
The 30-share blue-chip DAX index ended the floor session up 11.41 points at 2,638.45, its gains supported by a steady dollar and firm Bund futures, but amid moderate volumes.

Attention was firmly focused on the U.S. Federal Reserve's meeting later today amid broad expectations for a quarter-point rate rise -- an increase dealers said would be moderate enough to avoid panicking markets.

"We don't believe anything too dramatic on rates can happen before the (U.S. November 5) election for political reasons. On the other hand, something serious could happen after then," one Frankfurt trader said.

December DAX futures followed the trend higher, gaining 12.5 points to 2,654.5. The dollar, while lower than Monday's levels, traded comfortably above the 1.5100 level and was seen as offering some support to shares.
Chemical group Schering AG gained 3.15 marks to 116.45 on some buying interest after news it was partnering Denmark's Novo Nordisk in fertility product research.
BASF AG, Bayer AG and Hoechst AG also gained, as traders said there had also been a small resurgence of the takeover talk that has long focused around the chemical sector.
Deutsche Bank AG rose 47 pfennigs to 72.37 after First Boston reiterated its buy recommendation for the stock.
